intervals.label: proposed experiment (planning phase)
intervals.note: Start is the arXiv submission of the first DELight paper (22 Sep 2022). The 2025 version of that paper still says 'DELight is currently in its planning phase'; the HEiKA STAR demonstrator funding of 2025 is listed on the official news page.
intervals.quote: The new ``Direct search Experiment for Light dark matter'', DELight, will be using superfluid helium as active target, instrumented with magnetic micro-calorimeters.

intervals.label: funded: DFG Research Unit 6006 (design, build and operate phase I)
intervals.locator: official news page, 'DFG Research Unit Funding - March 2026'
intervals.note: Funding award to design, build and operate phase I (official page, March 2026; KIT press release of 2 April 2026). Not 'construction': the KIT release says only that a cryogenic platform is being built in Heidelberg and that the experiment 'is being set up in an underground laboratory' (not named there).
intervals.quote: The Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) - German Research Foundation has awarded DELight the funding to design, build, and operate Phase-I of the experiment within the framework of the DFG Research Unit 6006

placements.note: Phase-I placement at the Vue-des-Alpes underground laboratory (new Atlas facility and site created for it; see the log).
placements.quote: In phase-I, DELight will be located at the Vue-des-Alpes (VdA) underground laboratory [18], a shallow lab in Switzerland with 230 m of rock overburden (∼630 mwe).

target_medium.quote: DELight employs a superfluid helium-4 target instrumented with Large Area MicroCALorimeters (LAMCALs), based on Magnetic MicroCalorimeter (MMC) technology.

summary.plain: A cell of superfluid helium surrounded and topped by wafer-sized magnetic thermometers that register the energy of a possible dark matter collision.
summary.technical: ~1 L superfluid 4He cell (first cell planned at 10 L in earlier papers) with about 50 sapphire-wafer LAMCALs (40 cm^2 each), SQUID readout, film burner, dilution refrigerator at ~10 mK.

technology.quote: DELight employs a superfluid helium-4 target instrumented with Large Area MicroCALorimeters (LAMCALs), based on Magnetic MicroCalorimeter (MMC) technology.
technology.value: Superfluid helium-4 target instrumented with large-area magnetic microcalorimeters (MMC)
